title: Hierarchical Mesoporous Carbon/Silica Nanocomposites from Phenyl‐Bridged Organosilane
material_description: (unlabelled 1) | mesoporous carbon obtained by HF removal of the silica from the mesoporous carbon/silica composite (carbonization of OTAB/1,4-bis(triethoxysilyl)benzene phenylene-bridged silica hybrid, 900 C, N2, 4 h); plotted as curve c in Figure 7
purification_method: silica removed by washing with dilute HF (~10 wt.-%) for several days
source_location: main.pdf p.4 (Adv. Mater. 2005, 17, 707), text paragraph on Figure 7: 'mesoporous carbon shows ... 1.2 wt.-% at 850 mm Hg and 77 K'; same measurement as last marker of Figure 7 curve c
notes: Printed pressure 850 mm Hg (113 kPa); converted 850 x 0.00133322 bar. Printed as 'calculated hydrogen-adsorption capacity'. digitized: 1.12904 bar, 133.886 cm3(STP)/g, archive: HYC-0126_fig7_curve_c_edge_marker35.json (marker 35 of 35, partly hidden by the plot frame; x position biased low by clipping). Surface area 850 m2/g, pore volume 0.50 cm3/g and average pore diameter 2.5 nm are from the N2-sorption isotherm of Fig. 6 (method not named; stored as headline area with surface_area_method=unspecified); TGA in O2 shows 97% weight loss (Fig. 4 curve b) so the sample is about 97 wt% carbon. H2 isotherm measured at 77 K on a Micromeritics ASAP 2010 analyzer; the paper does not say whether the method is volumetric or gravimetric and does not name the uptake basis; measurement_method=unknown.
